properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. @ajs, 2026-10-14: "I have a friend (Chris), who is a counselor at a university. He asked me: [...] If a state institution deploys AI that is biased against non-secular viewpoints and research, does the institution risk violating the 1st amendment and the establishment clause? [...] I feel like Chris could "design an argument for and against" using flo2.io."

As relayed, Chris's own framing is C. S. Lewis's The Abolition of Man: a small set of "conditioners" shaping what a generation believes and values. A trained, biased AI could be a vehicle for that. A chat model told him it is biased against Lewis's works because of its secular training.

OPTIONS, none chosen:
(a) CHRIS DESIGNS IT HIMSELF, in his own flo2 design, with his own chat app, through the flo2 connector.
(b) @ajs sets the design up with him, and Chris carries it on.
(c) A STRUCTURED TRIAL, as the three-agent trials ran (owner, designer agent, observer). Chris owns the design; an observer records where the vocabulary fits and where it fights an argument.
(d) NOT THIS QUESTION FIRST. Start with a less contested argument, so the trial tests the tool rather than the topic.

PUSHBACK, RECORDED BESIDE IT:
- IT IS CHRIS'S ARGUMENT. As with Emily's pieces, he designs it and nobody builds it for him. The tool's job is to hold both sides and their sources, not to argue either.
- THE CONTESTED TOPIC IS ALSO THE BEST TEST. Chris's worry is that the model is biased, and the model is what helps him build the design. That is exactly where showing what the person said apart from what the agent supplied matters (dec:idea-what-did-the-agent-infer-provenance-per-field-per-type-and-as-a-report, settled 2026-10-13, not yet built). An agent that supplies objections to one side only would show as an imbalance he can see. Counter: until that read is built, the imbalance is visible only to someone reading node by node. So (c) or (d) may need to wait for it.
- NOT LEGAL ADVICE. An argument map about the Establishment Clause is analysis. The design should say so, and every legal source (cases, statutes, the institution's policy) must be a cited document, never a citation from the model's memory, which is a known way AI fails in law.
- HE NEEDS A flo2 ACCOUNT. Who can get one is still open in flo2's design (dec:idea-who-can-get-a-flo2-account); so far accounts are family.
- IT IS ABSTRACT. Ideas, premises and objections have no build step and no test that runs. The trial would show where the "delivered" and "verified" readings mean something for an argument and where they mislead, which is its value as a trial.

SIZE, PLAINLY (a finding): no engine work for (a) or (b); an account for Chris; (c) costs a trial's observing time; (d) costs nothing but delays the interesting case.
properties.name: OPEN — should Chris's question be the first trial of designing a line of reasoning: he designs an argument for and against, in his own design on flo2.io?
properties.rationale: A real person with a real question that is exactly the class the parent idea describes, and one where the tool's honesty about who supplied which claim is the point. Recorded so it can be chosen or set aside on its own. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
